brief:
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached record highs, driven by optimism about megacap tech stocks and declining oil prices.

S&P 500 (+0.58% to 7818.93): S&P 500 Reaches Record High. The S&P 500 rose to a record high as investors became more optimistic about the outlook for megacap tech stocks [3]. The rally was driven by a decline in oil prices and yields, which made equities more attractive [4]. This move suggests that traders are watching the impact of rising interest rates on the stock market and are looking for signs of resilience in tech stocks [1, 2].
Nasdaq (+0.45% to 27599.89): Nasdaq Reaches New High. The Nasdaq rose to a record high as tech stocks lifted the market, despite high treasury yields. This move is attributed to the strong performance of megacap tech stocks, which drove the index to new heights. Traders are watching the market's reaction to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions, which may impact the broader market. [5]
10-Year Yield (-0.79% to 5.27): Oil Prices Slide, Treasury Yields Fall. Traders are watching oil prices as they slide, which led to a decrease in Treasury yields. This move is likely due to the expectation that lower oil prices will lead to lower inflation, which in turn will reduce the likelihood of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates. As a result, investors are selling bonds, causing Treasury yields to fall.
USD/JPY (+0.27% to 158.4): USD/JPY Surges Above 158. The USD/JPY pair surged above 158 as investors sought safe-haven assets amid rising US yields, which revived dollar buying. Traders are watching the Bank of Japan's cautious stance, which may limit its ability to intervene in the market. This cautious approach has offset concerns about Japan's intervention risk, lifting dollar demand and supporting the USD/JPY pair.
Crude Oil (+0.82% to 90.16): Crude Oil Prices Rise. Crude oil prices rose despite a report that Middle East crude exports are increasing, as traders are watching the potential for disruptions in Hormuz shipping. [16] The WSJ reported that the G-7 plans to release crude and diesel from stocks, but the risks of Hormuz shipping persist. [19] This move may be driven by concerns about home heating oil prices, which are soaring due to household expenses reaching a breaking point. [19]
Gold (+0.23% to 4166.3): Gold Prices Rise Amid Investor Uncertainty. Gold prices rose overnight as investors monitored domestic and global conditions, with traders watching for updates on gold mining company Q3 earnings and M&A activity. [20] [21] [22] The forecast of gold prices reaching $5,013 per ounce in 12 months from Investing.com also seemed to support the price move. [22] However, Reuters noted that price uncertainty was a challenge for gold M&A deals, which may have contributed to the cautious tone in the market. [23]

Also worth knowing:
- The S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit record highs as Nvidia and AMD led tech stocks higher, driven by cooler yields.
- The S&P 500 and Nasdaq joined the all-time-high territory, with the S&P 500 posting its first close above 7,800.
- Jim Cramer's top 10 things to watch in the stock market on Tuesday included a focus on tech stocks and earnings reports.
